citation.title: A deep Convolutional Neural Network for topology optimization with strong generalization ability
citation.authors: Yiquan Zhang, Bo Peng, Xiaoyi Zhou, Cheng Xiang, Dalei Wang

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The trained CNN produces a topology in 0.001 s on average, compared with 3.913 s for conventional SIMP on the tested problems.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 5 reports 3.913 s for SIMP and 0.001 s for CNN; 3.913/0.001 = 3913 [inferred]. Training and data-generation time are excluded explicitly.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and conclusion claim qualitative speed gain; Table 1 reports 99.97% calculation time saved and 4.16% mean compliance error, excluding disconnected cases.

baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Core i7-8700K CPU and NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti GPU machine; device used for SIMP not specified (Section 5)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Core i7-8700K CPU and NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti GPU machine; device used for inference not specified (Sections 4.1, 5)
baseline.training_time: not stated; validation loss stabilizes at about 50 epochs (Section 4.2.2)
baseline.quality_metric: Finite-element compliance error, pixel-value error, volume-fraction error, disconnection percentage (Section 5, Tables 1–2)
baseline.quality_gap: 4.16% mean compliance error, 0.13% mean volume-fraction error, and 4.12% disconnected test structures; compliance average omits disconnections (Section 5, Table 1).

R1.evidence: Section 5 and Table 1 compare 0.001 s inference against full SIMP runs despite 4.16% mean compliance error and 4.12% disconnections; no matched-quality timing is attempted.

R2.evidence: Section 4.1 uses the 88-line educational MATLAB SIMP implementation. Section 5 identifies a shared CPU/GPU machine but does not specify each method's actual device or a strong classical solver comparison.

R3.evidence: Section 5 explicitly excludes the time to generate 80,000 SIMP targets and train the CNN, with no cost numbers or break-even calculation.

R4.evidence: Section 5 and Tables 1–2 report compliance of returned structures, volume-fraction error, and percentages of disconnected designs; disconnected designs are excluded from average compliance and separately counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: 8,000 in-distribution test cases (Section 5); 8,000 each for two other support conditions (Section 6)

notes: Reported speed-up is derived from rounded average times. The abstract's speed comparison is qualitative; the conclusion and introduction also have no quantitative own-method timing comparison, so Section 5 supplies the primary outcome.
